summary: Helen Moore Johnson was an Indologist who earned degrees at Missouri and Wisconsin, also studying at Tulane, Bryn Mawr, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. She held posts at Oxford College for Women, Oxford Female Institute, and Johns Hopkins (1924–1936).

Helen Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She studied at SOAS University of London and became Curator of East Asian Money in the Department of Coins and Medals at the British Museum around 1991.
Helena Blankleder works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1979 to 1984. She held a post at Rice University beginning around 1987.

Helena Willman-Grabowska was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Jan Baudouin de Courtenay, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, Louis Finot, and Antoine Meillet at Paris, Bern, and Lausanne. She held positions at Paris, the EPHE, and Jagiellonian University (1927–1948).

Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich under Helmut Hoffmann and served as an editorial consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1964.
Hellfried Dahlmann was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Marburg from circa 1934 to 1948 and at the University of Cologne from circa 1948 to 1973.

Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm earned his doctorate at Berlin under Otto Franke after studies at Frankfurt, Kiel, and Grenoble Alpes. He taught at Peking University (ca. 1933–1948) and held the Lehrstuhl für Sinologie at the University of Washington (1948–1971).

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg, completing his PhD there around 1945–1948, and studied under Paul Debes in 1945. He served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from around 1952 to 1988.

Helmer Smith worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Uppsala and under Johansson, Andersen, Bloch, Pischel, and Geldner. He served as Docent of Indology at Lund (1921–1935) and Professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Uppsala (1936–1947).
Helmut Arntz was a linguist who studied under Hermann Hirt between circa 1930 and 1936. He held an academic post at the University of Giessen from circa 1935 to 1945.

Helmut Eimer was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hamburg, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Bonn, completing his doctorate under Frank-Richard Hamm in 1974. He held a position at the University of Bonn from circa 1974 to 2001.

Helmut Hoffmann was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Freiburg and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He held posts at Berlin, Hamburg, the University of Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980), and chaired the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.

Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed his doctoral studies and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He taught at Vienna and directed the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (2007–2014).

Helmut Nespital was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and Charles University under Vincenc Pořízka. He held posts at Humboldt University, the University of Bamberg, and the Free University of Berlin as professor of Indology.

Helmut Rix, a linguist and Indologist, earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg and habilitated at Tübingen, where he studied under Karl Hoffmann. He taught at Augustana Divinity School and Tübingen before holding professorships at Regensburg (1966–1982) and Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner. He served as assistant and associate professor at Vienna (1981–2015) and as Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmut Uhlig was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Vienna. He worked as a teacher at Volkshochschule and became director of Volkshochschule Tempelhof in 1956.

Helmuth Peter Holler was a religious studies scholar and Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and Kiel University. He served as principal of Rajahmundry Seminary (1897–1900) and founded and served as professor and principal at Oriental University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Bonn, Berlin, Tübingen, and Munich under Hermann Jacobi and others. He held chair positions at the University of Königsberg (1928–1944) and the University of Tübingen (1946–1959).
